'''Bjørn Pedersen''' (25 March 1933 – 1 March 2024) was a Norwegian chemist. He was research leader at SI (which later merged with [[SINTEF]]), and was professor of chemistry at the [[University of Oslo]] for 24 years. He also served three years as pro-rector at the university.

==Life and career==
Born in [[Vestre Aker]], Pedersen graduated as a [[dr.philos.]] from the [[University of Oslo]] in 1964, and subsequently worked as a researcher and eventually research leader for [[SINTEF|Sentralinstitutt for industriell forskning]] (SI). From 1979 to 2003, he was appointed professor in chemistry at the University of Oslo. His research included contributions to [[solid-state chemistry]], and the fields of [[electron paramagnetic resonance]] spectroscopy and [[nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy]].<ref name="snl">{{cite encyclopedia |title=Bjørn Pedersen (kjemiker) |encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]] |publisher=Norsk nettleksikon |location=Oslo |url=https://snl.no/Bjørn_Pedersen_-_kjemiker |access-date=29 April 2021 |last=Lykknes |first=Annette |author-link=Annette Lykknes |editor-last=Bolstad |editor-first=Erik |language=no}}</ref>

From 1985 to 1988, he assumed the position of [[List of rectors of the University of Oslo|pro-rector]] at the University of Oslo. As a writer, he issued the textbook ''Generell kjemi'' in 1998.<ref name=snl/>

Pedersen received an honorable doctorate from [[Uppsala University]] in 1989 and became an honorary member of the [[Norwegian Chemical Society]] in 2014.<ref name=snl/>

Pedersen died in [[Oslo]] on 1 March 2024, at the age of 90.<ref name=snl/>
